title: Olivia Colman and Alexander Skarsgård on Playing a Fisherwoman and a ‘Very Sexy Basket’ in ‘Wicker’: It’s ‘Two Souls Being Kind to Each Other’
description: Ever since its premiere at Sundance, “Wicker” has been generating headlines. Mostly thanks to its erotic scenes featuring Olivia Colman and Alexande
body:
Ever since its premiere at Sundance, “Wicker” has been generating headlines. Mostly thanks to its erotic scenes featuring Olivia Colman and Alexander Skarsgård as her custom-woven lover, with both characters putting an enthusiastic spin on Taylor Swift’s “Wood.”

	The film’s raunchiness might have surprised some unsuspecting viewers at Zurich Film Festival. But Colman adored the script.


	“I’ve never read anything like it before. It’s in my top three scripts that I’ve loved and I’ve done,” she said at the fest, where it celebrated its European premiere.
	

	“It’s beautiful, funny and original. And yes, the only way you can sell it is by having a picture of Alex as a very sexy basket.”

	In “Wicker,” Colman plays a medieval fisherwoman who’s constantly ostracized – until she marries a wicker husband (Skarsgård), created by the basket weaver (Peter Dinklage).

	It’s directed by Alex Huston Fischer and Eleanor Wilson, and adapted from “The Wicker Husband” by Ursula Wills-Jones.

	While no stranger to risqué films thanks to “Pillion,” Skarsgård – better known for darker roles – had to embrace his softer side for a change.

	“To be honest, I found it terrifying. I feel way more comfortable playing dark, twisted, demented characters,” he said.

	“This was a departure and yeah, I was confused in the beginning about how to approach this. He’s so sweet, so tender and caring, and all those things that I can’t relate to personally.”

	The famed Wētā Workshop created his woven body.

	“It was extraordinary. It really was,” he said, recalling seeing it for the first time.
	

	“Wētā is behind ‘The Lord of the Rings’ and that whole universe. They wanted practical [effects], which was really exciting. This was not going to be a CGI version.”

	He added: “I’ll never forget the first time I saw the wicker husband at the workshop in Budapest, and looked at that version of myself. We’d done a bunch of tests and scans, but I was shooting something else and they were obviously in New Zealand. Then they built it. Stepping into it was also a way of finding the character because it defined his physicality and who he was.”

	Learning how to move was tricky, though.

	“It was glued to my face! It was crucial that [the mask] would move with my facial movements so that it wouldn’t be completely flattened, but that meant I had to exaggerate them. Al and Elle, our directors, kept saying that normal movements wouldn’t really register. At first, that felt a little strange, like you really had to overact. Luckily, we had a few days to perfect that.”

	Obviously, Colman has never acted alongside a similar costar.

	“I’ve never done it before, but we’re in that magical world where we’re just talking to each other. We got on very well, and giggled a lot. It was lovely to play those two people. Well, one person and a basket.”

	Despite its twisted premise, “Wicker” – whose humor echoes the madness of “Monty Python and the Holy Grail” – also takes a look at the institution of marriage and gender roles.

	“None of the women [in the film] have their own names, except for the fisherwoman, and she’s shunned and ostracized for being sort of ugly and smelly, and unmarriable. But she shows them,” noted Colman.

	“I like the fact that they are the only equals here. They support each other, listen to each other, take care of each other. It was really about these two humans – or, again, a basket – and two souls being kind to each other. We have no same sex marriages in this story, which I just realized and that’s a shame, but they’re kind to each other and that was the important relationship in the film.”

	Skarsgård added: “It commented on the patriarchy of our time and on the construct of marriage, but it was done with so much humor. And in a way that didn’t feel preachy or too on the nose.”
	

	“It was so tender, sweet, funny and irreverent, and with a subtlety to it. That’s what really spoke to me.”

	After all, it’s all about a girl, standing in front of a boy – or a basket – asking him to love her.

title: Prime Video International Boss Urges TV Industry to Embrace AI: ‘It Doesn’t Replace Imagination, It Amplifies It’
description:
Prime Video international boss Kelly Day has urged the TV industry to embrace change, including AI.

	Speaking at the Royal Television Society conve
body:
Prime Video international boss Kelly Day has urged the TV industry to embrace change, including AI.

	Speaking at the Royal Television Society convention in London, Day, who is VP for international at Prime Video and Amazon MGM Studios, listed the ways that AI is being used to speed up and bring down costs throughout the production pipeline, from pitching to pre-production.

	“For a studio like us, AI enables us to bring down the cost of production while maintaining quality, meaning more stories get made, more creative risks get taken, and more diverse voices get heard. That is not a threat to creativity. That’s creativity unleashed,” Day said, speaking to an audience of senior executives in the TV industry including BBC director general Matt Brittin and Sony Pictures TV international boss Wayne Garvie.
	

	“AI doesn’t replace imagination, it amplifies it,” she continued. “We’re not looking for an AI model to write the next ‘Fleabag,’ and by the way, I don’t think it could. But AI might help the person who does spend less time on admin and more time on the creative vision that makes a show like that sing.”


	Day pointed out that first-time filmmakers were generating concept art and short films that “bring their pitch to life” while Prime Video was using it to “transform the viewing experience” for its audiences via personalized recommendations, simplified synopses, spoiler-free summaries, audio descriptions and subtitles.

	She said that Prime Video’s YA series “Maxton Hall” was now using lip sync technology to synchronize actors’ lib movements with human dubbed audio in different languages.
	

	Most recently, we introduced lip sync technology on Maxton Hall, our most watched international original, which synchronizes actors’ lip movements with human dubbed audio.

	Day added that “ethical guardrails” were required in using AI, however, saying they “cannot be an afterthought, they have to be the foundation and that’s the approach we’re taking.”

	The theme of RTS’s 2026 convention, which is being hosted by Amazon, is “united in change, if not now, when?”

title: ‘The Platform’ Co-Producer David Matamoros of Doce Entertainment Spain Boards Matías Rojas’ ‘Dog Legs’ (EXCLUSIVE)
description: In one of the later deals pacted at the San Sebastian Festival, Spain’s David Matamoros of Doce Entertainment boarded Matías Rojas’s adaptation of C
body:
In one of the later deals pacted at the San Sebastian Festival, Spain’s David Matamoros of Doce Entertainment boarded Matías Rojas’s adaptation of Chilean cult novel “Dog Legs” (“Patas de perro”), joining four other producers from Chile, France, Germany and Colombia.

	With this, “Dog Paws” enters the final phase of its financing and is expected to shoot in Valdivia, Chile during the second half of next year. Chile’s ever popular Alfredo Castro (Pablo Larraín’s “The Count,” “The Club”) is attached to star.
	

	“Spain’s involvement decisively strengthens the project and puts us in a very strong position to complete its financing,” said Federico Durán, the film’s Colombian producer through his new company El Sol Ermitaño. Durán, who has produced such notable films as “The Squad” and “Alias María,” just won a major post production award for his WIP project “Lovers Go Home!” at San Sebastián.


	“’Dog Legs’ is an ambitious project, both technically and artistically, but it also aims to reach a broad audience,” he told Variety.

	Matamoros, whose credits include “The Platform” and “The Virgin of the Quarry,” was also a producer at Zentropa Spain, the company founded by Lars von Trier.

	Chile’s A Simple Vista, led by Tomás Gerlach, first began developing “Dog Legs” some four years ago. This year, Reality Films, the production arm of French distributor Epicentre Films, which distributes Colombia’s Cannes-winning film “A Poet” and submission to the 98th Academy Awards international feature category, came on board at the 76th Berlinale, joining German company Klinker Films, a co-producer of “A Place Called Dignity,” Rojas’ previous film.
	

	Visual effects will be handled by French company MPC, whose credits include Thomas Cailley’s “The Animal Kingdom,” winner of Best VFX at the 2023 Sitges Film Festival and the French César Awards.

	Rojas’s ties to San Sebastian run deep. He premiered his debut feature, “Root,” at the festival 13 years ago. He later returned to its Europe-Latin America Co-Production Forum with his second fiction feature, “A Place Called Dignity.”

	Throughout his career, he has presented his films and projects at major international festivals including Cannes’ Directors’ Fortnight, the Berlinale and the Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival (PÖFF).

	Published in 1965, “Dog Legs “is a landmark of Chilean literature…radical, powerful, and still deeply unsettling. Six decades later, its themes of exclusion, abuse and violence remain strikingly relevant. The story follows Bobi, a 12-year-old boy born with literal dog’s paws, hidden away by his family until Carlos, a lonely, childless man, takes him in. His act of compassion turns the town against them, casting Carlos as a madman and Bobi as a monster and setting them on a devastating path toward violence.

title: Durban FilmMart Head on Why This Year’s Event Is ‘Looking Inward’ as African Screen Industries Strive to ‘Create Solutions’ on Their Own Terms
description: The Durban FilmMart returns for its 17th edition with a full slate of conversations and events looking to build on the legacy of innovation, disrupt
body:
The Durban FilmMart returns for its 17th edition with a full slate of conversations and events looking to build on the legacy of innovation, disruption and industry-defining discussions at what is arguably the most influential film market on the continent.

	Running from Oct. 9 – 12, this year’s event is organized around the theme “Shifting Worlds, Turning Toward Ourselves,” a focus that Durban FilmMart Institute director Magdalene Reddy says was inspired by the pioneering Senegalese filmmaker Ousmane Sembène’s memorable assertion: “Why be a sunflower and turn towards the sun? I myself am the sun.”
	

	“We are very much looking inward [at this year’s edition],” Reddy tells Variety. “In a world where…everything is shifting, we find that, at this time, it’s important for us as the African cinema community to look at what we need to create systems that will work for us. How can we consolidate? How can we create solutions?”


	The four-day event features a wide range of panel discussions, masterclasses, one-on-one meetings and mentorship sessions designed to capitalize on a moment of unprecedented visibility — and unparalleled disruption — for the African screen industries.

	In a departure from previous editions, which ran parallel to the Durban Intl. Film Festival, this year’s DFM will open with a screening, of Rwandan debutante Marie-Clémentine Dusabejambo’s Cannes Caméra d’Or winner “Ben’Imana.” The film, an alumnus of DFM’s influential pitching and finance forum, was selected to highlight the event’s outsized impact on the African filmmaking community.
	

	“This was a DFM project. It was pitched at DFM two years ago, and they were able to win two awards at Cannes [including the FIPRESCI prize],” says Reddy. “For us, the celebration of hosting a screening at the market — which we’ve not done previously — is based on the fact that we want to show our local content in our local context.”

	A crucial pillar of every DFM is its influential Think Tank strand, whose conversations and conclusions often “become a blueprint for the next DFM and the direction which the industry is going,” according to Reddy.

	Central this year will be a closed-door session gathering key distributors, financiers and industry leaders looking to tackle some of the vexing challenges of film distribution on the African continent, which has been hit especially hard by successive waves of corporate consolidation in the global industry. Another session will focus on audience development, “trying to see how we can connect better with our local [audiences],” Reddy says.

	A backbone of this year’s event will be a spotlight on equitable co-production, with a series of sessions organized in collaboration with the European Audiovisual Entrepreneurs network (EAVE). Tackling knotty issues such as how to best incorporate inclusivity into financing, development and production, the conversations will address the systemic imbalances that face African producers when partnering with outside co-producers, “even when they are coming with the stories, coming with the IP,” says Reddy.

	“How can they go in as an equal partner? How can they sit confidently at the table, so they are engaging in a way that will benefit them? Engaging in a way where finances can still come back to Africa?” she asks.

	Collaboration is a theme across the Durban FilmMart’s various strands, with the event forging a wide range of partnerships with industry bodies such as EAVE; the Nature, Environment and Wildlife Filmmakers (NEWF); the Cape Town Intl. Animation Festival (CTIAF); Documentary Africa; The StoryBoard Collective; and the Ladima Foundation, which supports African women working in the film and television industries, and will launch an initiative to push for greater gender equity at African film festivals.

	“Collaboration is something that has underpinned all the work that DFM has been doing over the years,” says Reddy. “In order for the industry to survive, we need to be working together.”
	

	This year’s Durban FilmMart unfolds at a turbulent time for the host nation, whose screen industries have been “struggling,” according to Reddy, particularly with ongoing uncertainty around South Africa’s 25% cash rebate.

	To that end, leading South African policymakers are expected to be on hand at DFM, which will host a closed session for local industry to meet one-on-one with representatives of the influential Dept. of Trade, Industry and Competition, which manages the country’s rebate policy; the National Film and Video Foundation; and various local and regional film commissions.

	“For us as DFM, the platform that we create is a platform for filmmakers not just to create a community for the filmmaking industry on the continent, but also a space for filmmakers to connect with policymakers,” says Reddy. “A space for policymakers to understand what are the challenges, what are the issues our filmmakers are facing. We try to bridge that gap between industry and policymakers so we can create a conducive environment and ecosystem for our filmmakers.”

	That mandate, she adds, extends to DFM’s broader engagement with the African continent as a whole. “Last year’s theme was creating bridges, and that’s what we continue to do. Even though it’s challenging within the continent to work with each other, we are trying to find ways to do that.”

schema.headline: Durban FilmMart Head on Why This Year’s Event Is ‘Looking Inward’ as African Screen Industries Strive to ‘Create Solutions’ on Their Own Terms

title: Madrid Audiovisual Cluster Dives Deeper Into New Business Models, AI and Emerging Technologies at Iberseries & Platino Industria
description: The Madrid Audiovisual Cluster (MAC), an economic interest group comprising close to 100 Madrid-based companies, has put together a two-day industry
body:
The Madrid Audiovisual Cluster (MAC), an economic interest group comprising close to 100 Madrid-based companies, has put together a two-day industry networking and peer-learning program at the Iberseries & Platino confab, taking place over Sept. 29 – Oct. 2 in the Spanish capital.

	AI takes center stage again but the program will attempt to delve deeper into the hot-button topic this year, presenting eight industry case studies examining innovation across the audiovisual value chain.
	

	“While AI is a common thread running through the projects, the session takes a broader view of innovation, covering new business models, emerging technologies and evolving production and creative workflows,” said Teresa Azcona, managing director of the Madrid Audiovisual Cluster.


	“Together, they show how innovation is transforming the industry and opening up new opportunities across the value chain.”

	But as Iberseries & Platino Industria co-Director Samuel Castro pointed out: “The ability to create stories should always be based on a fully human, author-driven concept and development. AI should be used as a tool, not as an end in itself.”

	Under the banner Innovation ‘Case Studies in the Audiovisual Industry: New Business Models, AI and Emerging Technologies,’ the eight case studies will illustrate how companies are applying technology to address practical challenges across the industry. Running from 12:00 noon to 2:00 p.m. on Sept. 29, the workshop will feature eight case-study presentations, with approximately 12 minutes allocated to each.
	

	The next day, Sept. 30, takes in a conversation between producer Rosa Bosch and Tanja Meissner, Director of Berlinale Pro, which encompasses major industry platforms including the European Film Market, Co-Production Market, Berlinale Talents and World Cinema Fund.

	Case Studies:

	1. PLIA: Applying PLIA Technology to Script Breakdown, Pre-Production Planning and Production Tracking on “Playback”

	PLIA, an AI-powered production platform for film and audiovisual projects, has developed an integrated production-management solution designed to bring the information generated across the creative and production process into a single platform.

	The company will present its application on the feature film “Playback,” covering script breakdown, pre-production planning and production tracking. The platform brings together scripts, notes, budgets, location photography and production breakdowns, with the aim of streamlining information management across the production workflow.

	Presenting: Jose Velasco — CEO, PLIA

	2. TBS  (Telefónica Broadcast Services) Tech Brand Stories: From the Physical Studio to the Virtual Production Environment: Virtual Production, AR, Motion Graphics and AI

	TBS – Tech Brand Stories, formerly Telefónica Broadcast Services, is the Telefónica Group’s creative production company and audiovisual agency. The company operates across live production, broadcast services, branded content and entertainment, combining creative and technical capabilities. Its team of more than 450 professionals works across major sporting and live events as well as non-fiction, entertainment, documentary and current-affairs programming.

	The case study will examine the convergence of virtual production, augmented reality, motion graphics and AI, and how these technologies are being integrated into contemporary production environments.

	Alberto Gonzalo — Graphics SupervisorLuis Miguel Boedo — Technical Coordinator

	3. Hark Media – Go Global: When AI Learns to Move Us: Hybrid Dubbing for Global Distribution

	Go Global specializes in localization for the entertainment industry, providing translation, subtitling, dubbing and voice-over services to streaming platforms and production companies.

	The company will look at the emerging role of AI in dubbing and how hybrid workflows combining technology and human expertise could support the localization of content for international markets.
	

	Paula Ferrari — Founder & CEO

	4. Xpost Studios – Secuoya Content Group: Innovation in VFX and Post-Production Workflows

	Xpost Studios, part of Secuoya Content Group, is a Madrid-based post-production and VFX facility operating from Madrid Content City. Its infrastructure includes facilities for editing, color grading, sound post-production, VFX and digital workflows.

	The session will focus on the application of new technologies to VFX and post-production workflows, examining how innovation is changing the way content is processed and delivered.

	Marcos Requena — Post-Production Manager

	5. Story Pitcher: Connecting Audiovisual Creators and Producers Through a Digital Platform

	Story Pitcher has developed a digital platform designed to connect screenwriters, directors and other audiovisual creators with production companies and content platforms.

	Its model combines AI-powered matching with legal-protection tools, with the aim of facilitating more direct connections between creative talent and industry decision-makers.

	Frank Belyeu — CEO, Story Pitcher

	6. Mercedes Santalla: From Talent to Market: Strategy and Business for Creative and Technology Projects

	Creative strategist and talent manager Mercedes Santalla works with projects and talent operating at the intersection of creative practice and technology. Her session will examine the commercial and strategic considerations involved in taking creative and technology-led projects from development to market, alongside the evolving relationship between talent, technology and business.

	Mercedes Santalla — Creative Strategist & Talent Manager

	7. Scoutters – Scout & Film: A Digital Platform for Location Scouting and Production

	Scoutters is a digital location-search and management platform developed by Spanish company Scout & Film. Built on Scout & Film’s experience managing locations for film and advertising productions, the platform connects location scouts, agencies, production companies and film commissions with locations suited to their production requirements.

	The case study will explore how digital tools are changing the traditionally location-based process of sourcing, managing and presenting filming locations.
	

	Rubén Souto — Co-Founder, Scout & FilmJose Díaz — Co-Founder, Scout & Film

	8. HaMo – Paramotion Films: HaMo Real-Time Animation System: Digital Puppetry and Next Lab R&D

	Developed by Paramotion Films through the Next Lab Generation R&D initiative, HaMo is a real-time motion-capture system designed for 3D animation and digital puppetry.

	The system uses inertial sensors to capture an operator’s physical movements and Unreal Engine to transfer them in real time to a CGI character. The technology enables virtual characters to perform live alongside human presenters and audiences, with potential applications across studios, live events and social media.

	This case study will look at the development and practical application of the system as an example of R&D moving from prototype to production technology.

	Jose Luis Farias — CEO, HaMoAlfonso Fulgencio — CTO, HaMo

title: Mayor Zohran Mamdani Refuses Jimmy Kimmel’s Request to Text Trump a Selfie of Them
description:
“Jimmy Kimmel Live” is back in Brooklyn.

	The late-night show has returned to the New York City borough for a week of shows at the Brooklyn Academy
body:
“Jimmy Kimmel Live” is back in Brooklyn.

	The late-night show has returned to the New York City borough for a week of shows at the Brooklyn Academy of Music. It’s Kimmel’s eighth time filming “Live” in Brooklyn, the place he was born and spent his early years, and the comic is welcoming a number of heavy-hitting guests to his couch, from Howard Stern and Billy Crystal to Paul McCartney and Sen. Bernie Sanders (D-VT). He said the show received over 150,000 ticket requests, and kicked off his Brooklyn week with guests Pete Davidson and Mayor Zohran Mamdani, as well as a musical performance by TV on the Radio, celebrating the 20th anniversary of their celebrated album “Return to Cookie Mountain.”
	

	While there weren’t any stories involving an Oscar-winning actor exposing himself to Kimmel in a bathroom, the host was heckled by Matt Damon in a Boston Red Sox cap — on the eve of the Yankees/Red Sox AL Wild Card Series — who was joined by Kimmel’s mother and sister, and Jon Hamm, cosplaying as an angry New York City construction worker. After his sit-down interview with Davidson, who was promoting his Netflix video podcast “The Pete Davidson Show” and upcoming film “How to Rob a Bank,” Kimmel welcomed Mayor Mamdani to the stage. He prefaced his arrival with a montage of clips of Fox News talking heads predicting that New York City would become “terrifying” under Mamdani and crime would go “through the roof.” That proved to be wrong, as murders and shootings in the city hit record lows in Mamdani’s first seven months.


	“Another thing that is very unexpected is this relationship that you have with President Trump, which seems to be a very friendly relationship,” Kimmel said, adding, “Did you guys hit it off immediately or is it something that you really went into thinking, ‘OK, I need to have a relationship with the president of the United States, and I think the best way to do it is to charm him.’ How did you do that, and can you help me?”
	

	Mamdani laughed. “Sorry brother,” he replied. “The president and I have many disagreements. One thing we do agree on is this city, how much we love this city, so from that first meeting in November of last year, I was just thinking of how we can make this meeting not about us, but about New Yorkers. How can we spend that time talking about the things that can make life in the city a little bit easier.”

	Kimmel then threw to a video clip of Mamdani standing next to Trump at Gracie Mansion as the president gave a rambling speech, with the camera pressing in on Mamdani as he stood there stone-faced. “I mean, it is remarkable,” offered Kimmel. “I watch that, and I go, ‘OK, this is not a guy I’d want to play poker with.’” Mamdani said that while Trump is speaking, he’s only focused on getting federal approval for his proposed Sunnyside Yard project, a development in Queens that would feature an estimated 12,000 new homes and create approximately 30,000 jobs.

	“You text with the president, I’ve read?” Kimmel pressed further.

	“From time to time we’re in communication, and it’s about Sunnyside Yard, and it’s about how we can deliver for the city,” replied Mamdani. “One of the other things the president mentioned that we spoke about, that I care very deeply about, is Haitian New Yorkers. They’ve had their Protected Status ended, and I really believe we need to do whatever we can so they have stability. They’re part of the fabric of this city.”

	Kimmel then asked if they could text Trump “a selfie of us right now,” only to have Mamdani shut him down: “Jimmy, I love you, but I love housing more.”

schema.headline: Mayor Zohran Mamdani Refuses Jimmy Kimmel’s Request to Text Trump a Selfie of Them

title: Should the BBC and Channel 4 Merge? Sony Pictures Television’s International Production Boss Wayne Garvie Thinks So
description: The ongoing difficulties faced by the U.K.’s public service broadcasters could be partially alleviated by a dramatic merger between two of the four
body:
The ongoing difficulties faced by the U.K.’s public service broadcasters could be partially alleviated by a dramatic merger between two of the four main players, the BBC and Channel 4.

	Speaking at the RTS London Convention, Sony Pictures Television’s international production chief Wayne Garvie argued that for Channel 4 — the publicly-owned, commercially-funded network struggling with declining advertising income and rising costs — to survive, it should become part of the main national broadcaster. 
	

	“My view is that you put Channel 4 as the commercial arm of the BBC, doing public service commercial channels and bringing them together, and then Channel 4 could have its own identity,” he said on a panel  entitled The View From Our Window alongside Roku U.K. head Richard Halton and Hearst Network’s U.K. manager and EMEA chief creative officer Heather Jones. 


	“That’s what I would I do. I think it’ll probably happen, because frankly it’s very difficult to see how Channel Four survives in its present form. And it’s not it’s fault. It’s that the market is changing in every conceivable moment.”

	A potential merger between the BBC and Channel 4, which would be a monumental shakeup in the U.K. TV industry, has been mooted before. Back in 2024, reports emerged that the idea was being discussed, a move that at the was claimed would add more than $1.3 billion to the BBC’s coffers and enable Channel 4’s to cut costs, free up budget to be spent on commissioning new programmes and use its profits to subsidise other parts of the BBC.

	According to The Guardian, another reported model was for Channel 4 — which several years ago was under threat of privatisation by the then Conservative government — to operate as a semi-independent entity under BBC Studios, the BBC’s for-profit arm.
	

	At the time, a BBC spokesperson said there were “no ongoing discussions” about the merger of the BBC and Channel 4 “nor are we developing a proposal to do so.”

schema.headline: Should the BBC and Channel 4 Merge? Sony Pictures Television’s International Production Boss Wayne Garvie Thinks So

title: Jon Stewart Takes Aim at Trump’s Meeting With China’s President: ‘How Does America Even Stay on the Map?’
description: On Monday night’s episode of “The Daily Show,” Jon Stewart gave audiences a comedic rundown of the recent developments in the relationship between D
body:
On Monday night’s episode of “The Daily Show,” Jon Stewart gave audiences a comedic rundown of the recent developments in the relationship between Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping following Trump’s hosting of Jinping in Washington, D.C., for what was called a “reciprocal state visit” by the White House.

	Stewart kicked off his monologue by introducing the two and setting the scene of their time together.


	“Last week, a young man by the name of Donald Trump picked up a young man by the name of Xi Jinping, Chinese president, at the airport for a pivotal three-day visit to Washington. Now, as with any monumental meeting of superpowers, with profound repercussions for global safety and stability, it began with ‘House Tour,’” sang Stewart, before cutting to news videos of Trump pointing at a number of different areas.
	

	“Trump spent most of Xi’s White House visit just pointing at shit, while Xi did his best effort to pretend to be impressed. Although I’m sure they talked about issues of national importance,” said Stewart, then alternating to news clips of Trump speaking to the press: “We had a great meeting, and he has great interest in granite,” he said.

	“Does he? Does he love good granite?” asked Stewart. “Is that his ‘I love good granite face?’ Because it looks like his ‘I’d rather be standing in front of a tank in a square face… Like President Trump, I’m sure you’re proud of your new circular granite helicopter parking spot, but just so you know, this is Shenzhen, China. They’ve got a fully autonomous magnetic levitation train. Pretty sure he’s not blown away by carved rock in the shape of a circle.”
	

	Stewart continued, pointing out that Trump must understand “the seriousness of the competition between our two nations” and would not undermine America’s national security. “I mean, national security is the whole reason we’re paying $600 million for this ballroom, right? So you’ll keep that behind the curtain, yeah?” Not quite — Trump invited the couple “through that beautiful curtain,” making them the first people to set foot in it. “Maybe Trump’s just trying to sell Xi Jinping on renting the ballroom out for his next big function,” joked Stewart.

	He then brought up recent developments in China-U.S. relations, playing news clips explaining that China had been sending Iran weapons. And not only did this topic not appear to come up between the two presidents, but it seemed as though Trump offered to sell American weapons to China.

	“How does America even stay on the map sometimes? I don’t even. How do we not just slide into the sea? All right, I had to have misheard that. I got to hear it from the president himself.” The show then cut to a clip of Trump denying this, saying that China probably would like to buy weapons from the U.S., though, “because we do make better equipment.”

	Check out the entire monologue below.

schema.headline: Jon Stewart Takes Aim at Trump’s Meeting With China’s President: ‘How Does America Even Stay on the Map?’

title: ‘Avengers: Endgame Encore’ Tops U.K., Ireland Box Office
description: Disney’s “Avengers: Endgame Encore” dominated the U.K. and Ireland box office, debuting in first place with £4.1 million ($5.5 million) across its o
body:
Disney’s “Avengers: Endgame Encore” dominated the U.K. and Ireland box office, debuting in first place with £4.1 million ($5.5 million) across its opening frame.

	“Resident Evil,” distributed by Sony, moved to second position in its sophomore frame, collecting $3 million to elevate its running total to $11.6 million. Paramount’s action thriller “Heart of the Beast,” starring Brad Pitt and J.K. Simmons, bowed in third place with an opening haul of $2.8 million.
	

	Universal’s “Sense and Sensibility” opened in fourth position, generating $2 million in its debut frame. Studiocanal’s animated release “Shaun the Sheep: The Beast of Mossy Bottom” took fifth place in its second weekend, adding $1.1 million to push its cume to $3.4 million.

title: Dennis Haskins, ‘Saved by the Bell’ Star, Dies at 75
description:
Dennis Haskins, the actor best known for portraying Principal Richard Belding on “Saved by the Bell,” has died. He was 75.

	Haskins’ longtime agent
body:
Dennis Haskins, the actor best known for portraying Principal Richard Belding on “Saved by the Bell,” has died. He was 75.

	Haskins’ longtime agent, Jay Schachter, confirmed the news to Variety on Monday. A cause of death and further details have not been released at this time.

	“It’s a tragic loss,” said Haskins in a statement. “Everyone loved Mr. Belding and those of us who got to know Dennis loved him even more. He was a great person, and he loved, I mean absolutely LOVED his fans. He always had time for them, no matter what. He was my client and dear friend for over 20 years, and I will miss him terribly. I’m heartbroken.”
	

	Haskins played the iconic principal in the long-running series from start to end. The show ran from 1989 to 1992, and Haskins appeared in nearly 90 episodes. He also played Belding in “Saved by the Bell: The New Class,” the TV movie “Saved by the Bell: Hawaiian Style” and the precursor to the main series, “Good Morning, Miss Bliss,” which aired in 1988. 


	His character famously used the catchphrase, “Hey, hey, hey, what is going on here?” when trying to discipline Bayside High students Zack Morris, A.C. Slater and Screech Powers. He starred alongside Mark-Paul Gosselaar, Dustin Diamond, Lark Voorhies, Dennis Haskins, Tiffani-Amber Thiessen, Elizabeth Berkley and Mario Lopez.

	Haskins also appeared in a number of other films and television shows, including “Abstruse,” “A Million Ways to Die in the West,” “A Bennett Song Holiday,” “Trailer Park Shark,” “Jennifer Falls” and more.
	

	Dimples Karaoke, a bar in Burbank, Calif., shared a tribute on Instagram to the actor, who was a regular at the establishment.

	The caption reads: “Dennis was a staple at Dimples. A lot of people thought he owned it, but he didn’t. He just loved the place and its people. He enjoyed singing for people, meeting them, and taking selfies with his fans. Dimples closed down about 11 years ago, and people still associate him with his beloved ‘second home.’ He was known to most as Mr. Belding from Saved by the Bell, but to us, he was much more than that.”

	“Late last night, that journey ended for him. He is now at peace and is probably entertaining the people in the sky. Just know that if you tried to reach out to him in the last few years, I did read your messages to him, and you were heard.”

            Renée Zellweger can breathe a little easier … she's been dismissed from a lawsuit brought by a house guest who claims she was injured at her boyfriend's rental home ... TMZ has learned.
      
    
            According to court docs, obtained by TMZ, Tracey Belland dropped the Oscar-winning actress as a defendant in her $10 million lawsuit. The lawsuit against Renée was dismissed with prejudice, meaning it can't be refiled.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            Tracey sued Renée and her boyfriend, Ant Anstead, over an alleged 2024 incident that happened at a home he was renting in Laguna Beach, CA. The woman claimed she hurt herself after stepping on a thin rug that was covering a hole, causing her to stumble and fall and injure her knee.
      

            Sources previously told TMZ that Renée had nothing to do with the rental and was not on the lease … and had her own place nearby.
      
    
            Ant denied all allegations that he was legally responsible for the woman's injuries.
      
    
            The case against Ant is ongoing.

title: Lindsay Clancy Holdout Juror Speaks Out for First Time After Mistrial
description:
Lindsay Clancy Holdout Juror
                          Take Focus Off Me and Back on Getting Just
body:
Lindsay Clancy Holdout Juror
                          Take Focus Off Me and Back on Getting Justice!!!
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              September 28, 2026
                            7:43 PM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The lone holdout juror in the Lindsay Clancy murder trial is breaking his silence following the dramatic mistrial ... and he's asking the public for one wish, to shift its attention away from him and back on the 3 young lives lost.
      
    
            Michael Desronvil appeared on Fox News' "Hannity," where he addressed the intense fallout surrounding the jury's deadlock and the criticism he's faced since the case ended without a verdict.
      
    
      
      🚨🚨🚨BREAKING: The lone holdout juror in the Lindsay Clancy mistrial, Michael Desronvil, has broken his silence in a video statement sent exclusively to Fox News' Sean Hannity."I know the whole focus has been on me, but we want to reel everything back and put the focus on the…
              @mikerreports
  
    
            The juror states in the brief video "I know the whole focus has been on me, but we want to reel everything back and put the focus on the three angels."
      
    
            Desronvil became the center of attention after jurors deadlocked over whether Clancy was legally responsible for the deaths of her three young children.
      

            The jury ultimately failed to reach a unanimous decision, prompting a judge to declare a mistrial ... however, during his video appearance on "Hannity," Desronvil made it clear he doesn't want the story to be about him.
      
    
            Instead, the criticized juror pointed viewers back toward Lindsay's late children Cora, Dawson and Callan Clancy -- the three lives at the heart of the case.
      
    
            The juror has faced public criticism from fellow members of the panel, who accused him of refusing to accept their interpretation of the evidence and the law. Desronvil has denied those allegations.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The explosive jury dispute came after days of deliberations in the Massachusetts case. Clancy admitted killing her children but pleaded not guilty by reason of insanity ... with her defense arguing that she was suffering from severe mental illness -- including postpartum psychosis -- when the killings occurred.
      
    
            Prosecutors argued she remained legally responsible for her actions. Now, with the case ending in a mistrial, attention has turned to what happens next ... including whether prosecutors will pursue another trial.

title: Cornell Student Diego Sarabia Loses Wells Fargo Job Amid Alleged Sexual Assault Case
description:
Alleged Cornell Gang Rape
                          Accused Student Canned from Wells Fargo
body:
Alleged Cornell Gang Rape
                          Accused Student Canned from Wells Fargo
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              September 28, 2026
                            5:07 PM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Diego Sarabia, one of the Cornell students accused of sexual assault, is suddenly out of a job at Wells Fargo as prosecutors reopen their investigation of the alleged 2024 incident ... TMZ has learned.
      
    
            Sources with direct knowledge tell TMZ ... Sarabia is no longer employed at the Charlotte, NC bank branch where he'd reportedly been employed since 2022. We're told the decision was directly tied to the Tompkins County D.A.'s announcement Monday his office is considering criminal charges.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Sarabia is one of seven Cornell alums and fraternity brothers named in a civil lawsuit filed by a Jane Doe. She claims she was drugged and sexually assaulted at the Chi Phi fraternity house in October 2024.
      

            According to the lawsuit ... Doe had been drinking at Moonies Bar & Nightclub before making her way to the fraternity house. She claims she was visibly intoxicated -- and underage at the time -- but Moonies employees still served her alcohol.
      
    
            Moonies has denied the allegation, telling TMZ its staffers marked the hands of underage guests and gave wristbands only to people who were 21 or older. The establishment says bartenders were instructed to serve alcohol only to customers wearing wristbands.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            The lawsuit claims a Chi Phi member later sent a crude Snapchat message -- "free p***y" -- to invite other frat brothers to join in on the alleged assault. Jane Doe claims multiple men entered the room, including Sarabia, who allegedly grabbed her face and kissed her as she tried to hide under the covers.
      
    
            She also claims the men plied her with ketamine while sexually assaulting her.
      
    
            The Tompkins County D.A.'s Office did not charge anyone when Doe initially reported the alleged incident -- but, the prosecutor said Monday he was reopening the criminal investigation, and plans to present the case to a grand jury.
      
    
            No criminal charges have been filed yet, but for Sarabia, the fallout has begun.
      
    
            We've reached out to Wells Fargo and Sarabia ... so far, no word back.
